notes: Only DirectDrawCreate is an import: everything else is a COM method the guest reaches through the vtable, which the host dispatches from crates/web-host/src/shim/ddraw.rs. Entries carrying an object are documented here and are not emitted into the import table. The palette methods are what the screen fades run on, so they are the part that must be exact.

functions.name: DirectDrawCreate
functions.description: Hands back the one DirectDraw object. Null GUID means the primary driver, which is the only one this host presents.
functions.evidence: trace: called once during startup, immediately followed by SetCooperativeLevel

functions.name: SetDisplayMode
functions.description: Records 640x480x8 and refuses any other depth loudly: the page presents an 8-bit indexed surface and a 16-bit request would otherwise be silently misread.
functions.evidence: trace: (640, 480, 8) once at startup and again after the display mode is restored

functions.name: SetCooperativeLevel
functions.description: Stores the flags (exclusive vs normal) because the game queries them later when it decides whether to clip the pointer.

functions.name: CreatePalette
functions.description: Allocates the palette object the fades write through. The guest immediately calls SetEntries on it, so a null palette here breaks every fade in the game.
functions.evidence: trace: one palette created per screen that fades

functions.name: CreateSurface
functions.description: The primary and back surfaces. The surface's pixels come out of the host arena, which is why a released surface must really free them or a board session runs out of memory.
functions.evidence: trace: two surfaces at startup, one extra per screen transition

functions.name: SetEntries
functions.description: The fade primitive. Every fade in this game keeps the same frame and rewrites palette entries only, never flipping, so the host must bump its palette revision here or the page repaints the old frame and the fade is invisible.
functions.evidence: trace: 256 entries rewritten per fade step, no Flip between steps

functions.name: Flip
functions.description: Presents the frame and increments the flip counter the page watches. A screen that only fades presents once, which is why the flip count alone is not enough to drive repaints.
functions.evidence: trace: 1 flip for the logo screen, 30-60 per second in the board

functions.name: Blt
functions.description: Copies sprites into the surface with the colour key applied. This is the busiest call in the game and the one a port would optimise first.
functions.evidence: trace: thousands per frame on the board screen

functions.name: WaitForVerticalBlank
functions.description: Succeeds without waiting: the page's own frame callback is the vsync. Sleeping here would stall the interpreter for a frame on every call.
functions.evidence: trace: called before each Flip in the board loop
